ended: Won the NBA Finals over SA

archetype.name: Champion (frontcourt-driven)
archetype.definition: A team that was very good rather than dominant over 82 games, then played like the league's best team for two months and won the title, 16-3, behind a frontcourt that graded A+.

report.headline: A good regular season became a 16-3 title run carried by the frontcourt

recap.finish: 53-29, second in the Atlantic; won the NBA Finals 4-1 over SA
recap.body:
The Knicks spent the regular season as a clear contender without looking like the clear favorite. They finished 53-29, three games behind Boston in their own division, with a Net Rtg of 6.5 that ranked 5th. The profile was balanced: the 3rd-ranked offense (119.8 ORtg), the 7th-ranked defense (113.3 DRtg), a slow Pace of 96.8, and some of the best rebounding in the league. They grabbed 76.7% of opponents' misses (2nd) and 29.3% of their own (5th). Their record also understated them. The W vs Pt Diff of -3 says the margin was worth 56 wins, not 53.

The season came in waves. A 2-3 October gave way to an 11-3 November and a 10-4 December, which put them at 23-10 and looking like the East's best team. January was the soft spot: a 7-8 month in which the offense fell to 110.13 points a game, the lowest of any full month. The defense held up through it, allowing 107.2. February (8-4) and March (10-6) were steady more than spectacular. The defense kept tightening, with allowed points per game dropping below 109 in each of the final three months. A 5-1 April closed it out, even with a three-game road losing skid at the end of March.

The engine was the frontcourt. Karl-Anthony Towns ranked 4th of 95 on his tab and led the team with 9.5 Win Shares on a 61.9 TS %. OG Anunoby added All-Defensive Second Team defense and the best On-Off on the roster (+5.1). Mitchell Robinson posted a 67.6 TS % and a 3.5 BPM in limited minutes. Opposing centers managed 17.3 points a game against them, the fewest in the league. Jalen Brunson carried the scoring load (1,927 points on a 30.4 USG %) and made All-NBA Second Team. The rest of the backcourt was thin enough to drag the group to a C.

The postseason was a different team. Atlanta pushed them early: after a Game 1 win, they dropped Games 2 and 3 by a point each, 106-107 and 108-109, before closing the series with wins of 114-98, 126-97 and 140-89. From there they swept Philadelphia and Cleveland, winning all eight games, several by blowout margins. They beat San Antonio 4-1 in the Finals. That series was a grind, with wins of 105-104, 107-106 and 94-90, but the close games that cost them in the regular season went their way when it mattered. Their playoff Net Rtg of 15.5 led all postseason teams, as did their eFG % (56.6), REB % (54.3) and Opp 3P % (31.4).

The frontcourt pair turned a good team into a dominant one. Anunoby shot a 72.1 TS % with a 9.4 BPM in the playoffs. Towns matched that 9.4 BPM on a 68.4 TS %, with a team-best +12.3 On-Off. Brunson raised his usage to 32.6% and scored 539 points. The title is the top of a steady climb: playoff wins went from 0 in 2021-22 to 6, 7, 10 and now 16.

highlights.title: Towns and Anunoby owned the playoffs
highlights.body: Both frontcourt starters posted a 9.4 BPM over 19 postseason games, at a 72.1 TS % for Anunoby and 68.4 for Towns, and the team was +12.3 per 100 with Towns on the floor. That is far above even their strong regular seasons, so some of it is a hot two months, but it rests on a group that graded A+ over 82 games.

highlights.title: Rebounding and interior defense as foundation
highlights.body: The Knicks finished 2nd in DRB % and 3rd in REB %, and held opposing centers to the fewest points in the league. That kept the defense among the league's best despite middling perimeter numbers. It is structural, not streaky: they led the playoff field in REB % too.

highlights.title: A defense that improved year over year
highlights.body: Def Rank rose to 7th from 14th the year before, and Net Rtg rose to 6.5 from 4.2, without giving up the top-five offense. The postseason defense was better still: 100.95 points allowed a game, with opponents shooting 31.4% from three.

lowlights.title: Backcourt depth graded a C
lowlights.body: Brunson was an All-NBA guard, but the minutes behind him were weak, and the backcourt grade landed at C. Jordan Clarkson ranked 93rd of 144 at his position with a -3.3 BPM and -3.2 On-Off. Even Brunson's own On-Off was -2.3. This is the clearest gap on a title roster.

lowlights.title: Close games cost the division
lowlights.body: The margin was worth 56 wins, but they won 53, a W vs Pt Diff of -3 that ranked 24th. Boston won the Atlantic by three games. The same pattern showed up in 2023-24, so it is a recurring leak rather than one bad year, though it reversed in the Finals.

lowlights.title: No free throws, loose perimeter defense
lowlights.body: Their FT Rate of 23.8 ranked 24th, so the offense lived on jumpers and putbacks rather than the line. Opponents shot 36.2% from three (20th). The playoff Opp 3P % of 31.4 looks more like a favorable run than a fixed problem, and these numbers could easily drift back next season.

arc.note: A hot November and December built a 23-10 start. A 7-8 January dented it, and the team steadied through spring on a tightening defense. It then peaked in the playoffs, going 12-1 after falling behind 1-2 to Atlanta.

recap.nextYear: What carries over is the core: Towns (9.5 Win Shares), Brunson (8.8), Bridges (8.0, all 82 games), Anunoby and Hart, plus a frontcourt and wing group graded A+ and A-. The rebounding and interior defense are the most durable parts of the profile. What needs work is the guard rotation behind Brunson, which graded a C, and a perimeter defense that ranked 20th in Opp 3P % over the full season. Some of the title run will not repeat: a 15.5 playoff Net Rtg, 31.4% opponent three-point shooting and three one-possession Finals wins all ran hot. A W vs Pt Diff of -3, on the other hand, suggests the regular-season record could rise even if the underlying team stays about the same.
